replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: I actually checked this one before recording. Current B.C. and UBC pronunciation guides render Stó:lō roughly as “Staw-lo,” although I’ve also seen older guides use “Stoh-lo.” There seems to be some variation in how it’s written phonetically for English speakers, but thanks for mentioning it.

replies.text: There is a recent 'politically correct' motivation saying that the Clovis people came across the Bering Strait and not Europe. This is being pushed even in wikipedia. It is false. DNA evidence shows there are ancient strands in the First Nations people but that is only because some bred with the European Caucasian Clovis after they conquered them. replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: The genetic evidence doesn’t support that. DNA from the 12,600 year old Clovis-associated Anzick individual shows that Clovis people were closely related to present-day Indigenous peoples of the Americas, not European Solutreans. The Solutrean hypothesis has not been supported by ancient DNA.
